items.title: Three patterns every vector database should handle
points: Three core AI patterns—RAG (Retrieval-Augmented Generation; a technique that grounds AI model outputs in your actual data rather than relying only on pre-trained knowledge), agentic memory, and semantic search—each require different vector database (a database that stores and searches data as numerical vectors representing meaning) capabilities.
RAG grounds models in your actual data, agentic memory provides persistent cross-session memory for AI agents, and semantic search matches user intent rather than exact keywords.
Architecture, not feature checklists, should be the primary criterion for selecting a vector database since each pattern demands different capabilities.

Evaluation framework includes four factors: hybrid search (combining keyword-based and vector similarity search), scaling and hosting trade-offs (managed/vendor-operated vs. self-hosted), metadata filtering (filtering by attributes like date or document type alongside semantic matches), and embedding pipeline fit (how well the database integrates with your process for converting raw data into vectors).
AWS Marketplace offers an evaluation guide with architecture diagrams and free trials to test vector databases against specific workloads.

sections.title: Vector Database Evaluation Framework
points: 1. Hybrid search capability: the database must support both keyword-based and vector similarity searches together, not just one.
2. Scaling and hosting trade-offs: evaluate whether the database handles your data growth and whether you prefer managed (vendor-operated) or self-hosted deployment.
3. Metadata filtering: ability to filter vectors by associated data attributes (like date or document type) alongside semantic similarity matching.
4. Embedding pipeline fit: how well the database integrates with your existing process for converting raw data into vectors (numerical representations that capture semantic meaning).
